🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON INVENTS A "LEFT-WING TERRORISM" — MEXICO REFUSES TO PLAY ALONG</u>

Mexico refused to attend Marco Rubio's summit against "left-wing terrorism," invoking Article 89: non-intervention. A new Contralínea analysis lays out what Washington is actually selling.

"First they invent a threat through persistent discursive operations; then they offer the antidote," writes Fernando Buen Abad — backed by consultancies, military corporations, digital platforms and surveillance labs.

The elastic label exists to merge social protest, unions and disobedient governments into a single enemy.
banner: US INVENTS 'LEFT TERRORISM' — MEXICO OPTS OUT

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN VICECONSUL IN BARCELONA ACCUSED OF SEXUAL ASSAULT; SRE ON NOTICE</u>

A criminal complaint in Spain accuses Mexico's viceconsul in Barcelona, Priscila Martínez Carbajal, and her partner of sexually assaulting a young consulate contractor in December 2025 — Contralínea obtained the filing. The SRE says it is in contact with the victim.

The case lands on a damning pile: 167 complaints filed with the SRE Ethics Committee against Mexican foreign service officials between 2022 and 2025, including sexual harassment and violence.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CONGRESS SUMMONS CHIHUAHUA GOV. MARU CAMPOS OVER FORCED DISPLACEMENT OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES</u>

Mexico's Congress is done waiting on Chihuahua's PAN governor. The Comisión Permanente votes Wednesday on a summons for Maru Campos over forced internal displacement in the Sierra Tarahumara: more than 1,000 people driven from 4 municipalities and 13 localities in 2021, with 1,500 more forced out by 2024, per INEGI and Conapo figures cited in the ruling.

The Rarámuri people face "a structural crisis of security and human rights" that even drew in the UN refugee agency.

PAN and PRI voted against the measure.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>CUBA RESISTS: "SILENT GENOCIDE" DENOUNCED FROM MEXICO</u>

On the 73rd anniversary of the Moncada assault, Mexican solidarity organizations and the José Martí Association of Cubans Resident in Mexico gathered in Mexico City with one message: Cuba is enduring a "silent genocide."

"Not with bombs like Gaza, but a silent genocide where an entire people — 10 million Cubans — is denied the minimum conditions of life," said Olivia Garza, the association's vice president, citing blackouts of over 25 hours a day and more than 120,000 patients waiting for hospital care.

The blockade is the weapon. Resistance is the answer.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO'S POWER GRID SMASHES ALL-TIME RECORD: 54,300 MEGAWATTS</u>

El Financiero reports the National Electric System hit a historic peak of 54,300 MW at 8:22 pm Thursday, breaking the record set in June 2023. CFE infrastructure director Juan Francisco Cuevas says the driver is big industry, data centers and the digitalization of the economy. Nearshoring is now visible on the load curve — and the public grid is carrying it.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>SHEINBAUM DELIVERS HOMES, DEEDS AND CREDITS IN MORELOS; HOUSING GOAL RISES TO 24,000</u>

In Xoxocotla, President Sheinbaum delivered Fovissste settlements, INSUS property deeds and new homes under Vivienda para el Bienestar, and Morelos confirmed the land is ready for 24,000 houses across 11 municipalities — 75,000 of the national 150,000 already assigned in 119 municipalities. Her words: "The governments before took from the people; we raise the minimum wage, deliver homes with accessible credits and take the debt off families. They governed for a few — we govern by the people and for the people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>HOW NEOLIBERALISM ERASED THE SOCIAL ECONOMY FROM MEXICO'S CLASSROOMS</u>

Contralínea rescues Sarah Babb's study of UNAM economics theses: from the 1940s to the 70s the dominant authors were Marx and Keynes; by the "lost decade" of the 80s the syllabus belonged to Hayek and Friedman. Political economy gave way to sterile econometrics — and the social economy of cooperatives and collective enterprise was simply deleted from the curriculum. What neoliberalism expelled from the university is now rebuilding itself in public policy.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MURDERED MORELOS MAYOR WAS HIMSELF UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR CARTEL TIES: HARFUCH</u>

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch revealed that Valentín Lavín, the Temoac mayor killed inside his own city hall, was being investigated for links to the Los Aparicio / Los Huazulco cell — and for possible intellectual participation in the murders of activists Samir Flores and Sandra Camacho. His mother-in-law "La Patrona," the municipal treasurer, is already detained as an alleged operational leader. In Mexico, investigations don't get buried with the bodies.
banner: TEMOAC MAYOR WAS UNDER CARTEL PROBE

🇲🇽📚 <u>"HATE SPEECH IS NOT JUST AN OPINION": MEXICO'S SCIENCE CHIEF TAKES ON THE FAR RIGHT</u>

At a Secihti forum on the far right as a political phenomenon, Secretary Rosaura Ruiz drew the line: when discourse slides into hate, exclusion, racism, misogyny or historical denialism, "hate speech is not simply opinion" — it legitimizes discrimination and opens the door to violence. Her diagnosis, for Mexico and the world: the far right "is no longer marginal; it has begun displacing the traditional right."
banner: SECIHTI: FAR RIGHT NO LONGER MARGINAL

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICANS FEEL SAFER THAN AT ANY POINT IN THE SHEINBAUM ERA: INEGI</u>

INEGI's ENSU survey puts urban insecurity perception at 59.8% in June — the lowest reading since Sheinbaum took office, down from 61.7% in December 2024 and 63.2% a year ago. Ciudad Nezahualcóyotl collapsed from 55.5% to 41.3% in a single quarter; Nuevo Laredo is down to 26.5%. Homicides cut in half, and now perception follows. The "failed state" headline writers will ignore this one too.
banner: INEGI: SAFETY BEST OF SHEINBAUM ERA
